text:
Predicates:
Invertebrate(x) ::: x is an invertebrate.
Vertebrate(x) ::: x is a vertebrate.
Backbone(x) ::: x has a backbone.
Mating(x) ::: x reproduces by male-and-female mating.
Bee(x) ::: x is a bee.
Queen(x) ::: x is a queen bee.
Premises:
∀x (Invertebrate(x) ⊕ Vertebrate(x)) ::: Animals are either invertebrates or vertebrates.
∀x (Backbone(x) → Mating(x)) ::: All animals with backbones reproduce by male-and-female mating.
∀x (Vertebrate(x) → Backbone(x)) ::: All vertebrate animals have a backbone.
∀x (Bee(x) → ¬Mating(x)) ::: All bees do not reproduce by male-and-female mating.
∀x (Queen(x) → Bee(x)) ::: All queen bees are bees.
Bee(harry) ::: Harry is a bee.
Conclusion:
((Vertebrate(harry) ∧ Backbone(harry)) ⊕ ¬(Vertebrate(harry) ∨ Backbone(harry))) → ¬(Invertebrate(harry) ∨ Queen(harry)) ::: If Harry is either both a vertebrate and an animal with a backbone, or neither a vertebrate nor an animal with a backbone, then Harry is neither an invertebrate nor a queen bee.
